taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a shrub (FEIS, Anderson 2001).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: a shrub 1 m to 3 m high, as in the photos and on the bajada.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: up to 3 m to 5 m on good sites.

traits.life_span.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis: trees or shrubs.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: a spiny, intricately branched shrub.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: evergreen in the mild winters of the Sonoran Desert, though it sheds leaves in severe drought or frost.

traits.rosette.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: a spiny, intricately branched shrub, leafy along the twigs: no rosette.

traits.spines.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: plant a spiny, intricately branched shrub.

traits.bark_colour.note: Bark and branches smooth pale grey; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 96189411, 173845672, 101245394, 164622541, 394991184, 297384024, 258393089, 138338468): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.stem_clump.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: foothills and mesas, often forming dense thickets.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves alternate, as in the genus.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: leaf blades elliptic to oblong-ovate: simple.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: blades entire or sparingly crenate-dentate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 1.5 cm to 4 cm long, about twice as long as wide.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: leaf blades not more than 2 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: leaf blades elliptic to oblong-ovate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: blades rounded to acutish at apex.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: blades entire or sparingly crenate-dentate.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: herbage puberulent; the genus's leaf blades very rough above.

traits.inflorescence.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis: flowers axillary, solitary or in small clusters; drawn as small cymes.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flowers tiny, greenish; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 96189411, 173845672, 101245394, 164622541, 394991184, 297384024, 258393089, 138338468): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.sexual_system.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis: flowers perfect or unisexual: polygamous.

traits.fruit_type.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis: fruit a globular drupe with thin flesh and a hard-shelled stone.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis: fruit a globular drupe.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: drupes 5 mm to 8 mm across.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Drupes ripen bright orange, within the genus's 'yellow to dull red' (Kearney and Peebles 1942 p. 228); sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 96189411, 173845672, 101245394, 164622541, 394991184, 297384024, 258393089, 138338468): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowers in spring, March to May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: drupes ripen from July to October, after the summer rains.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: 1,500 to 3,500 feet: about 460 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: 1,500 to 3,500 feet: about 1,070 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: foothills and mesas, in the open and beside larger shrubs and trees.

traits.moisture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 228), Celtis pallida: foothills and mesas.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense, intricately branched shrub of smooth grey zigzag branches with short spines, small rough dark green leaves, and bright orange berries. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for desert hackberry from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of snowbrush ceanothus (ceanothus-velutinus); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 2.0 m tall at 15 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
